report.title: Bitwise wrapper operations preserve the underlying operator result
report.explanation: For endian-type 0.2.0, the handwritten BitAnd, BitOr, and BitXor implementations of BigEndian<T> and LittleEndian<T> apply the corresponding underlying T operator and wrap its successful output. Each of the six proved contracts quantifies arbitrary operand and output types, operands, and operator dictionaries: the translated wrapper result equals the underlying operator result. This includes propagation of failure or divergence represented in the Aeneas result model. The wrappers add no independent failure in that model. These contracts prove the unchanged published wrapper bodies; they do not prove any user-supplied T operator implementation.

report.title: Exact branch tests, payload projections and swapping in Either
report.explanation: For either 1.19.0, is_left and is_right report the actual variant for every Either value. left and right return Some of exactly the corresponding payload or None for the opposite branch. left_or and right_or return the matching payload or the supplied default. flip swaps Left and Right while preserving the payload; a separate composition theorem proves that flipping twice returns the original value. These seven original method bodies terminate normally in the Aeneas model for arbitrary payload types and values, without inspecting or modifying payloads.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library models and Lean kernel are trusted. Transitive theorem axioms are limited to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; no local trusted helper contracts or custom models are used.
report.limitations: Coverage is limited to the seven named methods and the two-flip composition. Closure-taking maps, iterators, pinning, borrowed mutable projections, formatting, serde and other trait implementations are not verified. Rust destructor behavior and resource consumption are outside the pure value model. Other targets and feature configurations were not checked.

report.title: Base16 buffer length calculations and odd-length rejection
report.explanation: For base16ct 1.0.0, decoded_len terminates normally for every input slice. It returns Ok of exactly half the input length when that length is even, and Err(InvalidLength) exactly when it is odd. It examines length only, so this result does not validate hexadecimal characters. encoded_len returns exactly twice the input length without a panic when the length is at most usize::MAX / 2. These are body proofs of the unchanged published length helper APIs, over arbitrary slice lengths representable in the model.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library slice/scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. The proofs add no local axioms or custom standard-library models. Transitive theorem dependencies use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
report.limitations: Only decoded_len and encoded_len are covered. Hexadecimal encoding, decoding, character validation, destination writes, allocation and encode_str's unchecked UTF-8 conversion are not verified. encoded_len behavior above usize::MAX / 2 is outside the proved precondition. Other targets, feature configurations and release overflow behavior were not checked.

report.title: Exact bit reading and bit setting for u8
report.explanation: For bit_field 0.10.3, get_bit returns the requested bit for every byte and index 0 through 7. set_bit produces x OR (1 << bit) for true and x AND NOT (1 << bit) for false, with 8-bit operations, and returns a mutable reference to that updated byte. Its translated backward function is the identity: a later write through the returned reference updates the original byte to that value. Both unchanged method bodies terminate normally in the model on these inputs. One manual executable size_of::<u8>() = 1 model is supplied, with extraction guards restricting its use to the sole u8 instantiation. Kani independently checks the original Rust methods against the reference formulas and returned-reference behavior, and checks the u8 layout value.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, official scalar models, Lean kernel, and Kani/CBMC are trusted. One manual executable external model supplies size_of::<u8>() = 1. Its generic Lean signature comes from extraction but does not model arbitrary types: guards inspect all serialized LLBC functions and generated Lean modules and reject any non-u8 size_of call or additional translated methods. Kani checks the Rust u8 layout value; its correspondence to the Lean model is a reviewed bridge, not an in-Lean proof of Rust standard-library layout. Public theorems use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
report.limitations: Only the u8 implementations of get_bit and set_bit at valid indices 0 through 7 are covered, on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu with default features and debug overflow checks. Invalid indices, other integer types, get_bits/set_bits, BitArray methods, other targets and release behavior are not verified. No generic size_of property is established. Kani uses a different Rust nightly from Aeneas extraction; its layout and body checks do not prove the extraction toolchain itself.
